parsed.explanation: The combined regime splits sharply. State level is documented top-tier: 1993 gender-identity protections, hate-crime coverage, open marker changes, X on licences, care coverage, conversion-therapy ban, shield law, 'most protective tier' (July 2026). Federal level imposes operative traveller-facing exposures: binary-only visa/passport markers (SCOTUS-allowed Nov 2025), a cable directing refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex plus possible lifetime fraud findings, trans-athlete visa bans, documented border detentions prompting eight foreign advisories, federal-facility exclusion, hostile custody policies and documented abuse of trans immigration detainees. Federal border and custody authority overrides state protection for those stages; state protection holds for daily life. Net: functioning acceptance with a real, unremedied federal exclusion-and-detention edge.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal Feb-2025 order and Nov-2025 Supreme Court ruling bar X markers and self-selected sex on passports/visas; Feb-2025 cable directs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, flags possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, bans trans athletes; travellers report blocked/confiscated passports and border detentions.
entry_documents.protection: State issues X on licences/ID with no documentation, open birth-certificate marker changes; legal-aid FAQ on document rules; ACLU suit pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal border authority is exclusive; the state's open document regime cannot cure a visa refusal or secondary screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented border detentions over visa issues (triggered eight foreign advisories); trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair, hormones, psychiatric drugs) from 2026.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State anti-discrimination and hate-crime law; state shield law barring enforcement of out-of-state warrants/extraditions over lawful care; courts functioning.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy can move a visitor from the protective state sphere into federal custody where hostile policies operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities, reaching federal buildings and programmes inside this state; 15+ states have bans, 4 criminalise in some circumstances, one state arrested a trans woman in March 2025.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state has no facility ban (most-protective tier) and its 1993 public-accommodations law covers gender identity in private and state venues.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection covers daily venues; federally funded facilities remain excluded regardless of state law.

care_services.exposure: Federal DOJ subpoenaed 20+ hospitals for under-19 patient records (2025); funding freeze; proposed public-insurance bar for under-18 trans care; clinical chilling risk for visiting families.
care_services.protection: State public insurance covers trans care, bars insurer exclusions, codified 2023; shield law protects families travelling for treatment; conversion therapy banned.
care_services.interaction: Shield neutralises out-of-state process but not federal investigative or funding power reaching providers serving a visiting minor.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' ideology; DOJ reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology'; EO directs police investigation of schools facilitating social transition; agency purge of 'gender' terms.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State repealed trans-panic defence (2024), has gender-identity hate-crime penalties since 1993 and broad non-discrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing raises outing and hostility probability even where state institutions protect.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal EO calling minor gender-affirming care 'mutilation', directive to criminally prosecute teachers facilitating social transition, record subpoenas and proposed insurance bars create investigation and care-denial risk for a visiting family; school facility bans in other states.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law expressly bars removal of children from parents over lawful care, protects families travelling for treatment, bans conversion therapy for minors, covers care in public insurance.
minors_guardians.interaction: State shield covers custody process from other states; federal investigative and funding instruments are not shielded against.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence figures for residents or visitors; national bias statistics cover sexual orientation only.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate-crime penalties since 1993; trans-panic defence abolished; non-discrimination law since 1993; national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Enforcement data absent, so actual operation of the protective machinery is unverified.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, executive-order challenges and health rules unresolved; shield law untested against a specific out-of-state order; no enforcement data on hate-crime/non-discrimination provisions; federal remedies in flux.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, pending litigation, functioning state courts, July-2026 risk map's most-protective rating.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies do not reach federal border or custody decisions, where exposure concentrates.

anchor_checks.comparison: Materially above: 0.15-B features routine border detention, months-long court failure and capital-adjacent decrees. Here no offence criminalises trans identity, state courts protect, and custody abuse is confined mainly to immigration custody rather than routine entry; but unlike 0.15-B the federal entry edge is documented, so the gap is one of frequency and state complicity, not absence.

Closest fit: secondary screening, discretionary refusal of entry, administrative rather than criminal penalties, appeals slow and rarely revised. This dossier matches that border tier while adding stronger state-side protection than 0.55-B, offset by documented trans-detainee abuse and hostile federal framing — pulling the two ways to a similar net level.

Below: 0.75-A has care access with functioning enforcement and no entry-side restriction. Here the operative federal layer adds document-based refusal, possible lifetime ineligibility, federal-facility exclusion and conversion-style custody policy — tier-1/tier-2 exposures 0.75-A lacks, which the state layer cannot remedy.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets two systems. Inside the state, documented machinery works in her favour: long-standing non-discrimination, hate-crime penalties, open marker changes, X on licences, care coverage, a shield law protecting families travelling for treatment, and a top-tier July-2026 risk rating — supporting reduced-to-low-risk daily life. At the border and in federal custody, the operative regime is hostile: binary-only markers, a cable directing refusal on sex discrepancy, possible lifetime fraud findings, athlete visa bans, documented detentions, federally funded facility exclusion, and severe reported abuse of trans detainees. Federal authority is exclusive at those stages, so state protection evaporates exactly where severity peaks. For an adult alone or with a minor, entry is the acute exposure; staying clear of federal facilities and carrying consistent documents materially shapes risk.
